title: Thirty-one killed in massive fire as fuel tanker crashes on Cairo highway
description: Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health minist
body: Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says.Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening.Unverified footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead.The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation.It then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire, the state-owned newspaper says.Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas and often run-down infrastructure making incidents more common, the response to which is often complicated by slow emergency response times and locally improvised rescue efforts, even in the sprawling Egyptian capital.Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished, as emergency services blocked off entry routes.

schema.headline: Thirty-one killed in massive fire as fuel tanker crashes on Cairo highway

title: Andy Taylor obituary: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a Wild Boy on stage and off
description: In 2022, it was announced that he had advanced prostate cancer, the same disease that had killed his father. Le Bon spoke for the remaining members of
body: In 2022, it was announced that he had advanced prostate cancer, the same disease that had killed his father. Le Bon spoke for the remaining members of the group. "It's absolutely devastating," he said.Taylor avoided chemotherapy, believing it would affect his guitar playing by weakening his fingers. Instead, he embarked on an experimental "nuclear therapy", which he hoped would give him five more years of life.Initially, at least, it seemed successful but, a year later, Le Bon said his former bandmate's disease was a  "very late, fourth-stage metastasised cancer".In 2025, Taylor managed to release a third solo album, Man's a Wolf to A Man. Urged by Tracey to express himself for a final time, he even provided the vocals.For Andy Taylor, that first train ride down to Birmingham had been like entering Narnia in the Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe.Overnight, he had gone from serenading strippers in northern clubs to a rock-star lifestyle with the world's most popular band.So, was the rollercoaster ride worth it? Taylor answered his own question in his autobiography, published in 2008."Maybe if there'd been fewer lows there wouldn't have been so many highs," he wrote. "If I had to do it all over again, I don't think I would have changed a thing."Though next time I'll give a miss to swallowing all that elephant's piss," he added.

schema.headline: Andy Taylor obituary: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a Wild Boy on stage and off

title: Trump’s accounts traded Nvidia shares 44 times this year, records show
description: Image source, ReutersByThomas Copeland and Alison BenjaminBBC VerifyDonald Trump's investment portfolios have bought or sold shares in chipmaker Nvidi
body: Image source, ReutersByThomas Copeland and Alison BenjaminBBC VerifyDonald Trump's investment portfolios have bought or sold shares in chipmaker Nvidia at least 44 times this year, a review of the US president's financial disclosures shows.Trump's most recent public declarations of his investment trading show that between January and September the portfolios purchased between $5.2m and $17m (£4m and £13m) in Nvidia stock - and sold between $4.4m and $12m. His portfolios held between $12.5m and $58m of Nvidia shares at the end of 2025.Financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics report a low and high range of transaction values, so a more precise analysis of how much Nvidia stock was traded is not possible.The period of recent turmoil at Nvidia and volatility in its share price is not covered by the disclosures. In the last two weeks, co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang resigned and then Trump played a significant part in his reinstatement.The White House has said that Trump's stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third parties and neither he nor his family "has any ability to direct, influence or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold".Huang resigned on 12 November after reports of extramarital affairs, including with one woman who has alleged ties to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia's share price dived following news of his resignation.But on Monday Nvidia's board announced the 63-year-old was being reinstated as CEO.Trump told US media he had "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to bring Huang back. The board said it had "received input from senior levels of the United States government" that he posed "no national security risk".Nvidia's share price surged 31% on Monday following Huang's return. About $1tn (£763bn) was added to Nvidia's market value, but the company's shares are still trading below their value before reports of Huang's alleged affairs began to circulate.However, concerns remain among both Republican and Democratic politicians about Huang's actions and Nvidia's compliance with US controls over the export of advanced computer chips to China, as well as Trump's involvement in getting him reappointed as CEO.Image source, Getty ImagesNvidia's chip technology and investments have been critical to the growth of the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, leading to it becoming one of the world's most valuable companies.The firm now represents more than 6% of the S&P 500 share index, according to State Street financial services. This makes it the second most valuable company on the index after Apple, whose shares Trump's accounts also frequently trade.Nvidia also ranks highly in many global indices, meaning that investment accounts held around the world, including pensions, are likely to include its shares.Our analysis of Trump's Nvidia trades does not include other investment products held by him which may include its shares.Trump made at least $2.2bn (£1.7bn) from a variety of investments and commercial activities, according to the financial disclosure report for the first year of Trump's second term.Barbara Perry, a presidential historian at the University of Virginia's Miller Center, told the BBC there is "no precedent for this," adding: "It's beyond anything we've ever seen in the presidency."Additional reporting Becky Dale

schema.headline: Trump’s accounts traded Nvidia shares 44 times this year, records show

title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
description: The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy. The new taxes charged on imports
body: The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy. The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners - China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions.The move follows the White House's investigation into the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal.China is facing the highest rate of up to 40%, followed by Vietnam at up to 35% and then others facing either 20% or 25%. The new duties are not expected to take effect until next year.Tariffs are taxes levied on imported goods. The amount is typically calculated as a percentage of the good's value and paid to the government by businesses importing the products from abroad.Some of these rates will be effectively reduced because of caps on tariffs Trump has agreed to. Individual countries also face different levies.The proposed tariffs will affect China, the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan, and India.US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the latest tariffs issued would "level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy".He claimed that many of America's trading partners had "for decades" adopted industrial strategies which included "targeting manufacturing, wage and labor suppression" as well as "other market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favor while eroding America's manufacturing base".But economists have warned tariffs can fuel inflation and push prices up for consumers if businesses pass on higher costs, as well as dampen global trade.Trump has repeatedly threatened or imposed tariffs during his second term, arguing they will boost US manufacturing and create jobs.Despite a poor result for the Republican party in the midterm elections, the president has continued to press on with his flagship trade policy.Trump is also seeking to cut the US trade deficit - the gap between the value of goods it buys from other countries and those it sells to them.However, Stephen Brown, chief North America economist for Capital Economics, said the latest tariff announcement was "not as alarming as it looks", due to the taxes "essentially replacing" previously announced tariffs made in the summer."The increase in the effective tariff rate looks set to be a touch lower than we've been assuming for our forecasts, although the new tariffs will still provide a marginal boost to prices," he said in a note."The key message is that the additional tariff burden is likely to be small, especially as various goods... are also not subject to these new tariffs."The announcement is likely to increase tensions between the US and China, the world's two biggest economies, who remain locked in a trade dispute and the AI race.The two countries have also been embroiled in a tit-for-tat tariffs war, which is currently on hold.Despite last week's meeting between Trump and China's President Xi Jinping, the two sides made no announcement on the trade war truce, which is set to expire on 10 January.The European Commission rejected the new US tariffs, saying it would investigate the US's reasons for bringing them in. It pointed out that tariffs are limited to the 15% previously agreed.

schema.headline: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China

title: Wife drugged and raped by husband asked police if she was to blame, court hears
description: Warning: This article contains distressing contentA woman who had been drugged and raped by her husband for 20 years asked police: "Is it my fault he'
body: Warning: This article contains distressing contentA woman who had been drugged and raped by her husband for 20 years asked police: "Is it my fault he's done this?", a court heard.The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's right to anonymity, has admitted a litany of offences against her - including rape, administering a substance with intent and inviting 13 other men to join the abuse.Nine of those men have pleaded not guilty to sexual offences against her and are standing trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court.Giving evidence in court for the first time, the woman also said claims she had been "pretending to be asleep" during the abuse were a "load of rubbish".The victim, in her 60s, was formally interviewed by Greater Manchester Police on 7 November last year, around two weeks after officers had arrived at her family home to arrest her husband.In the interview, played to the jury, she told Det Con Anouska Barker: "I had no knowledge of what you told me had happened and I still can't believe it's true, and I think you have made a mistake."She told police at the time of her husband's arrest that as far as she knew, the pair had not had a sexual relationship for about nine years due to her experiencing symptoms of the menopause.The husband, she said, had never complained about it and the pair never discussed it.Asked how their sex life was before, the woman described it as "just normal, vanilla".Asked by Barker what her husband had "been like" in the years they had not been in a sexual relationship, the woman said: "Is this my fault? Is it my fault that he has done this?""Absolutely not, I don't want you to ever think that," Barker replied.Describing their relationship, she said they had been "a loving couple". "We did things together, we went out with other people. We've always had quite a lot of friends and a good social circle and done things."During the interviews she said she had never consented or agreed to anyone else being involved in their sex life, and it had never been suggested by her husband.After the jury were shown the video of her police interviews, the woman was asked to take the stand in the courtroom.Katy Thorne KC, representing 43-year-old paramedic Jonathan Kirk, said her client's case was that the victim had spoken to him and had her eyes open in the early hours of 17 August 2025 - when he allegedly raped her while she was unconscious in her bedroom. Thorne said: "If I were to suggest to you - you were pretending to be asleep?"The victim spoke calmly and directly and replied: "That's a load of rubbish is what I'd say."Thorne said that Kirk's version of events was that the husband had explained that "you two as a couple had a sleep fetish; you had been pretending to sleep", asking the woman: "Is that something you recall?The wife responded: "No."Judge Maurice Greene interjected and asked: "Do you have a sleep fetish?"The victim said she did not. The jury also heard another of the accused, taxi driver Philip Wild, claimed that the victim had "greeted him at the door" on the occasions he is alleged to have sexually assaulted and attempted to rape her, in August 2023 and February 2025 respectively.In response to Pierce Power, defending Wild, she said: "No. That's a lie".She was also questioned by the barrister representing Jordan Wallace, 31, who is alleged to have raped her on 4 May 2025.Rachel White, defending Wallace, said she was not suggesting the victim had been "telling lies" but said she may have "not remembered" speaking to Wallace."It didn't happen," she said.Counsel representing the other six men on trial did not ask questions.Earlier in the trial Louise Oakley KC, prosecuting, said the woman had been subjected to the "barbaric fantasies" of her husband for more than two decades."The sad reality of this case is that there are many, many men whose fantasy is an unconscious and unresponsive woman," she said."[The husband] found a large number of them."An investigation into his offending began after a team of undercover journalists in Germany infiltrated a channel on the messaging service Telegram which was being used by some men to share images of unconscious women appearing to be raped.One of the users was traced by police to the husband's address, where he was arrested in October 2025.Oakley said more than a million photographs and videos of his wife being abused were found on a Samsung mobile phone, which she described as a "confession booth" of his "darkest secrets".On trial with alleged "contact offenders" Wild, Kirk and Wallace are amateur football coach Alan Keelan, 42; recruitment consultant Mohammed Sabir, 28; sheet metal worker Richard Townsend, 37, and Robert Stewart, 70, who was retired.Also in the dock are Daniel Rayner and David Graves, described as alleged "non-contact offenders" because they did not physically attend the home address, who deny conspiracy to rape, conspiracy to assault by penetration and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent.Four other men; Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee in Scotland; Sean Peers, 38, from Stockport; Graham Brougham, 74, from Northwich in Cheshire, and non-contact offender Karl Lindsay, 55, from Taunton in Somerset, have already pleaded guilty to a number of offences.

schema.headline: Wife drugged and raped by husband asked police if she was to blame, court hears

title: BBC appeals against decision to allow Trump's $10bn lawsuit to go ahead
description: The BBC has lodged an "urgent" appeal against a US judge's decision to allow Donald Trump's $10bn (£7.6bn) lawsuit against the corporation to go ahead
body: The BBC has lodged an "urgent" appeal against a US judge's decision to allow Donald Trump's $10bn (£7.6bn) lawsuit against the corporation to go ahead. The US president is suing the BBC for defamation over the way an episode of Panorama edited a speech he gave in January 2021, shortly before the riot at the US Capitol.Earlier this month, a federal judge in Florida ruled that the defamation case could proceed after the BBC sought to dismiss it.The BBC has now filed an appeal with a higher court, saying there is a "complete lack of evidence" that anyone in Florida accessed the programme, and that the broadcaster made "rigorous and systematic efforts to prevent access to the documentary" in the US.A BBC spokesman said: "We are surprised and disappointed by the court's decision that this case should be heard in Florida."As we have made clear from the start, the BBC broadcast this documentary in the UK - and UK only. We did not show it in Florida, nor did any other broadcaster."Given the urgency of this issue, we are now requesting a higher court review the ruling."President Trump's lawsuit accuses the BBC of "intentionally, maliciously and deceptively doctoring" the speech he gave on 6 January 2021.The BBC has apologised for the edit in Trump: A Second Chance, which it said had given "the mistaken impression that President Trump made a direct call for violent action".But the corporation argued that the Panorama episode, which was broadcast in 2024, did not meet the legal criteria for defamation.Earlier this month, federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz found Trump's defamation allegations against the BBC sufficient for the case to continue, although he did not rule on the merits of the case.President Trump called the judge's ruling a "huge victory" in a post on Truth Social at the time.The BBC has now lodged an appeal with the US Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, arguing that the Florida court has no jurisdiction to hear the case.Trump has been ordered to answer questions under oath as part of the lawsuit by 22 January.Judge Kuntz has scheduled a trial date for the case for 3 May 2027 in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

schema.headline: BBC appeals against decision to allow Trump's $10bn lawsuit to go ahead

title: Gordon Ramsay to host Top Gear as show revived after Andrew Flintoff crash
description: Figure caption, 'Top Gear is back': Gordon Ramsay announced as new hostByIan YoungsCulture reporterUpdated 5 hours agoTV chef Gordon Ramsay is to lead
body: Figure caption, 'Top Gear is back': Gordon Ramsay announced as new hostByIan YoungsCulture reporterUpdated 5 hours agoTV chef Gordon Ramsay is to lead the new presenting line-up on BBC motoring show Top Gear, which is being revived four years after it was last on air.Ramsay will take the driving seat alongside as yet unnamed co-presenters when the show starts filming next year. It will return to screens in 2028.The long-running programme has been off air since 2022, when co-host Andrew Flintoff suffered serious facial and rib injuries after his open-topped three-wheeled car overturned at the show's test-track.In a statement announcing his new role, Ramsay said he wants to bring "a fresh energy and ambition" to the show's formula of being "surprising, entertaining and [with] just the right amount of chaos".Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Andrew Flintoff, Paddy McGuinness and Chris Harris hosted the show before it was restedTop Gear began in 1977 and became one of the BBC's biggest hits in the hands of Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May in the 2000s.They were replaced by hosts including Chris Evans and Friends star Matt LeBlanc, before Flintoff took over in 2018 with Paddy McGuinness and Chris Harris. But the show was "rested" after the former cricketer's crash in December 2022.Flintoff was dragged face-down underneath the Morgan Super 3 car for about 50 metres. "I thought I was dead," he told a Disney+ documentary last year.The BBC apologised and paid compensation to Flintoff following his crash.'Lifelong passion for cars'In Wednesday's statement, Ramsay said he has had a love of cars since he grew up near the Silverstone race circuit in Northamptonshire."I would climb over the fences and sneak in for a glimpse of the racing," he said. "That early excitement sparked a lifelong passion for cars, motor sport, beautiful design and extraordinary engineering."At its very best Top Gear has always been about the unexpected - surprising, entertaining and just the right amount of chaos."That's the spirit we want to build on, bringing a fresh energy and ambition to create something truly thrilling for a whole new generation of audiences."It's an incredibly exciting opportunity, and I genuinely can't wait to get started!"Image source, BBC StudiosFormer host Richard Hammond told BBC Radio 4's PM programme that Top Gear is "a grand old BBC stalwart"."It goes back decades. We had our tenure of it and did our thing with it and went a bit crazy with it, and it'll be another incarnation of it," he said. "And great. It's a long runner, it'll carry on."He said that he does not doubt Ramsay's credentials as a car fan, and joked that TV chefs "love three things: cooking - well in his case four - swearing, cooking, but also big watches and cars". Hammond was seriously injured in a crash while filming the show in 2006, but said it "doesn't have to be" a dangerous show.The BBC asked Hammond to return to the show for the new series, he said. "They did talk to me about it. They came to me about maybe getting involved in leading the new Top Gear, and I don't want to drag it back to what it was. That's why I didn't do it," he said.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Ramsay drove in a celebrity race in Lego-themed cars at the Las Vegas Grand Prix at the weekendRamsay, 60, owns an extensive collection of cars including multiple Aston Martins and Ferraris, as well as a Porsche, Land Rover and McLaren Senna.He has also appeared on Top Gear three times as a guest - in 2002, 2006 and 2017.The BBC's director of entertainment Ed Havard said: "Gordon's fierce and fearless approach makes him a natural fit, and we're thrilled that audiences will see him in the driving seat as the show speeds into its next exciting era."Suzy Lamb, managing director for BBC Studios Entertainment, added: "The return of Top Gear had to feel like a real TV event and Gordon fits the bill perfectly."He brings passion, mischief, genuine motoring credibility, and the kind of infectious competitive streak that defines the show at its best."She promised that it "won't be a nostalgic reboot" but will be a "bold and unmissable new chapter for the most entertaining motoring show in the world".Comedian Jimmy Carr was rumoured to have been in talks to join the hosting line-up, but was reported on Tuesday, external to have "pulled out".Top Gear is the second high-profile show involving Ramsay to have been announced in the past week.He has also been confirmed to star in a revival of Hell's Kitchen on ITV, hosted by Claudia Winkleman, more than two decades after he originally appeared on the celebrity cooking programme.

schema.headline: Gordon Ramsay to host Top Gear as show revived after Andrew Flintoff crash

title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk
description: Poundland has collapsed into administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk, after its owners failed to find a buyer to keep it in business.The retailer'
body: Poundland has collapsed into administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk, after its owners failed to find a buyer to keep it in business.The retailer's shops and distribution centres will remain open and continue to trade during the administration process with the business likely to be broken up and some of its stores sold off to rival retailers.Poundland's US owners held talks with several bidders over a last-minute rescue deal, but no agreement was reached.Poundland boss Barry Williams said in a note to staff that the board had "no alternative but to take this decision", but was making it with "sincere sadness and intense regret".He said the US owners Gordon Brothers had removed "all borrowing facilities and access to our bank accounts" on 27 October, and adequate funds had not been released since then to keep the business solvent."Under these circumstances, it is impossible for the board of directors to see how Poundland can continue to operate as a going concern," he added.Kelvin Blake, 62, who has worked for the firm for 25 years, and whose partner has been there 29 years, said he was feeling "down, depressed", and because of his age, feared he would not find a job elsewhere."We didn't want it, but it's come so now we've just got to face it and see what the future holds."My income's gone," he added. "Obviously, we'll be working until we're told to leave."Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Poundland was "part of the fabric of high streets and communities up and down the country".He said the news of it going into administration just weeks before Christmas would be "deeply concerning for workers and their families".He added: "While it is worrying, going into administration does give other potential buyers the opportunity to engage and we will work hard with all the relevant parties to ensure the best possible outcome."Alix Partners, which has been appointed as administrator, said they would look at all options for the business, "including sales of the business and its assets, either in whole or part"."We appreciate this is a deeply concerning time for all involved - customers, suppliers and, in particular, Poundland colleagues," they said.Gordon Brothers has been criticised over how it handled a potential sale of Poundland, with accusations the investment firm hoped to profit from selling off the chain's 600 shops and stock piecemeal after running it into the ground.Gordon Brothers, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied such claims.On the funding question, Gordon Brothers said it had loaned the firm £85m over a year to help save it from insolvency.But insiders critical of the US firm have said it stands to make its loans back and more from the insolvency process.Previously, Gordon Brothers netted millions from liquidating the stock of fashion retailer LK Bennett, and in insolvency fees.Labour MP Liam Byrne told the BBC the House of Commons' Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee will recall Gordon Brothers before Parliament - two weeks after Gordon Brothers representatives last appeared at the committee to answer questions about Poundland, and where MPs said they were "deeply concerned" about the business.Byrne said: "I am really worried that a 'greed is good' approach to business by its owners has forced [Poundland] into an administration." He added the committee wants to know "how much money they're ripping out and crucially, how do we make sure, as a country, that we don't have this kind of scenario unfold again".Gordon Brothers met Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds on Monday to update him on the progress.The firm said on Wednesday that despite the Poundland management bringing about a turnaround over the past year, the firm was "still vulnerable" to inflation and any downturn in sales or profit margin, and it had faced "several years of instability".A spokesperson added the firm's "thoughts are with Poundland colleagues".It said it had stepped in to take over the retailer in 2025 when it was struggling, and when "no-one else was willing to finance the business".One of the central stumbling blocks in negotiations to keep the business afloat was a shareholder loan Gordon Brothers inherited when it bought the business for less than £1 last year.Gordon Brothers was owed £22.5m of that loan, while the previous owner Pepco was owed £7.5m.Gordon Brothers rejected various offers to buy the business as a going concern with deals to pay off that loan.Irish firm Martin Property Group offered to pay off £5m of the loan up front, and defer the rest of the payments to 2030.London-based Xyra group offered £12.5m up front but ran out of time to get a deal over the line.German investment firm Zachert Private Equity is also understood to have made a late offer.All of these were rejected.The crisis at Poundland really came to a head over the past few weeks after Gordon Brothers restricted access to funds for day-to-day operations.This meant that stock at the retailer was not being replenished at the necessary pace in the vital run-up to the festive period.

schema.headline: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang
description: Remember the tech boss and his head of HR, both married to other people, who were caught on camera at a Coldplay concert with their arms wrapped aroun
body: Remember the tech boss and his head of HR, both married to other people, who were caught on camera at a Coldplay concert with their arms wrapped around each other?Their horrified reaction went viral, and the pair both resigned. Astronomer, the firm where they both worked, said their actions had fallen short of its standards.Compared with the scandal which has engulfed Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang in recent weeks, that Coldplay kiss cam moment now feels rather tame.Huang admitted to having had an affair, reportedly with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. There were suggestions that she may have been involved in smuggling Nvidia chips into China, in breach of a US export ban. Concerns about national security had reached the desk of US President Donald Trump. There were other stories about some of Huang's relationships with female colleagues.For most of us, that would without question amount to instant, and irreversible, dismissal.But while Huang briefly left the company, he was just as swiftly reinstated, and welcomed back with open arms. As I watched footage of him being greeted with cheers, applause, high fives and a big hug back at the company's HQ on Monday, I wondered how many disgraced bosses would kill to be in his shoes."Imagine being that Coldplay CEO reading all the comments on here about how it's OK if you're actually a good enough CEO," quipped menswear writer Derek Guy on X, external.So, the US AI sector relies on Nvidia, Trump is determined that the American AI industry needs to be the best in the world, and Huang is the only leader the company has ever known.  He's been at the helm for 33 years and he's a computer scientist himself, renowned for being very hands-on with the development process. (Whether the boss's input is always wanted is another matter, but it's always there.)Working for Huang isn't easy.Long hours are normal and negative feedback is often given in front of everyone else. When he wants something to happen, he doesn't stop until it does: one of his early ideas was to halve the chip production cycle, in order to get one step ahead of the competition with their longer lead times for orders. Lots of experts told him it couldn't be done. Until eventually, they did it.Not only does Huang have technical expertise, he's also a charismatic figurehead, representing Nvidia at events around the world in his trademark leather jacket, rubbing shoulders with world leaders, royalty, and fellow tech bosses. For many, he's become something of a cult figure. Nvidia sometimes sells limited edition clothing at conference pop up stalls. A jumper featuring a cartoon image of Huang costs $178 (£137).

schema.headline: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang

title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
description: Judges in Israel have suggested prosecutors drop bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially handing the caretaker prime minister a boost
body: Judges in Israel have suggested prosecutors drop bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially handing the caretaker prime minister a boost as he fights for his political survival.The judges told the attorney general that there was little chance of conviction in the first of three cases he is facing, in which he is accused of granting government favours in exchange for positive media coverage.They also questioned whether his actions amounted to criminal conduct in a second corruption case, and suggested prosecutors seek a plea deal in a third.Netanyahu has consistently denied the allegations against him and called on Wednesday for the trial to be ended "immediately"."Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family, my son," he said in a televised statement. "Ten years of incitement to hatred that wounds the soul."Netanyahu was first charged in 2019, but court proceedings have been prolonged in part by the recent Israel-Gaza war.The case now under serious doubt, known as Case 4,000, concerns an alleged "reciprocal arrangement" between Netanyahu and the controlling shareholder in Israel's biggest telecoms company. Both denied any wrongdoing.In a highly unusual step, a judging panel at the Jerusalem District Court summoned Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara on Wednesday to express their concerns. "The chances of conviction are low – to an extent that warrants reconsidering the matter," Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told her, Israeli media reported.The judges also cast doubt on whether Netanyahu's actions, which are subject to a second case – concerning another alleged quid-pro-quo with another media baron, known as Case 2,000 – met the threshold for criminality.While they left open the possibility of a conviction in the third case: Case 1,000, which alleges Netanyahu acted for the benefit of an Australian billionaire after being gifted cigars and champagne by him.However, the judges told the attorney general that, in the public interest, there needed to be a "rethink" in how the trial should move forward, Israeli media report.Baharav-Miara said she would consider the judges' recommendations.It has been six years since Netanyahu became Israel's first sitting prime minister to face a criminal trial. He has always claimed to be the victim of a political witch-hunt and said on Wednesday that the "fabricated cases" against him were now falling apart.The cases have continued to progress in court while Netanyahu remained in power throughout the war in Gaza, though judges agreed to reduce the number of hearings due to security concerns around the conflict.The accusations against him have rocked Israeli politics, fuelling already deep divisions. His trial has coincided with controversial, far-reaching judiciary reforms by Netanyahu's government.For his opponents, Netanyahu's fear of prison has distorted his decision-making as prime minister and made him especially dependent on his far-right coalition partners to remain in power.This latest development will give a boost to Netanyahu, whose political opponent Gadi Eisenkot is currently attempting to form a coalition government after an inconclusive general election last month.While Netanyahu's parliamentary bloc won more seats than that of his rival, both fell short of an outright majority. Israel's president has offered Eisenkot the first chance to form a new administration.Netanyahu remains subject to an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza, which he also denies.

schema.headline: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu

title: Mims Davies: People are profiting on my likeness for AI porn
description: A member of parliament whose name and image were used in AI content on porn sites said the issue could make women less likely to want to enter public
body: A member of parliament whose name and image were used in AI content on porn sites said the issue could make women less likely to want to enter public life.Mims Davies, the shadow Welsh Secretary, said she received an email in her parliamentary inbox which said "her likeness was found on forums in abusive and pornographic content".The Conservative frontbencher said people making money from deepfakes was "grotesque", urging people to report it if it happens to them so that "culprits can be held to account"."It's completely unacceptable, it's a violation and an outrage," she told BBC Radio Wales Breakfast.Deepfakes are videos, pictures or audio clips made with artificial intelligence to look real. It is illegal, external to share or threaten to share intimate photos or videos of someone without their consent, including through deepfake images. Davies said she had waived her right to anonymity to call for more resources to find and prosecute culprits. Ofcom, the communications regulator, said "significant action is being taken to tackle intimate image abuse" but added there was "more to do".Davies, MP for East Grinstead and Uckfield in East Sussex, said: "There are things you expect to be dealing with these days in public life and frankly this is not it. "This could be any woman. This could be anyone in politics, in business, or down in your high street. "We need to be able to protect ourselves from deepfakes."She added: "This is going to have an effect on our daily lives, on our lifestyles. We need an answer to this."There's a problem, a new frontier which we need to battle."She previously told the BBC she was spiked on a night out in 2019.An Ofcom spokesperson said: "Nobody should have to experience the trauma of having an explicit deepfake created or shared without their consent. "Under the Online Safety Act, tech firms must assess and mitigate the risk of UK users encountering illegal content like this on their sites and apps, and remove it quickly when they become aware of it."We've laid down clear expectations for how platforms should do this – including by using automated technology to deal with illegal intimate images – and we've driven some of the strongest changes of any online safety regulation in the world."We've also shown we'll take action if evidence suggests companies are falling short."In January, Ofcom launched an investigation into X over concerns its AI tool Grok was being used to create sexualised images.The regulator gave platforms until the end of September this year to take effective steps  to stop illegal intimate images and deepfakes from spreading.At the time, it warned that any firms which breached their duties would face fines of up to 10% of their global annual revenue.The Department for Culture, Media and Sport has been approached for comment.

schema.headline: Mims Davies: People are profiting on my likeness for AI porn

title: Hotels need minimum standards to keep women safe, committee told
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Hotel bosses and women's groups were invited to the committee after a series of media reports into room intru
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Hotel bosses and women's groups were invited to the committee after a series of media reports into room intrusions ByAlex MeakinSouth of EnglandHotels should face national minimum standards to protect female guests, witnesses have told a parliamentary committee examining safety in the industry.The hearing followed an independent review into security failings at Travelodge after a woman was sexually assaulted at one of its hotels in Maidenhead, Berkshire. The review's author, Paul Greaney KC, said room intrusions had become so common they were treated as something to be tolerated, while Travelodge's interim chief executive admitted the company had not taken guest safety seriously enough.Committee chair and Labour MP Olivia Bailey said the evidence showed not enough was being done to protect women and called for "concrete action".The one-off parliamentary session heard evidence from hotel chains including Travelodge, Premier Inn UK and Z Hotels, alongside women's safety organisations.Three women giving evidence revealed they had previously barricaded their hotel room doors to feel safer during their stays.UK Hospitality chief executive Allen Simpson also recalled inadvertently revealing the location of a domestic violence victim to their abuser while working as a hotel receptionist earlier in his career.Greaney's independent review, commissioned by Travelodge, found the company had failed the Maidenhead victim "at every stage".The woman had spoken to the BBC after her attacker gained access to her room by lying to reception staff.Other guests subsequently came forward with similar experiences of security problems at Travelodge and other hotel chains.In August, Travelodge's chief executive Jo Boydell stepped down ahead of the publication of the independent review.Greaney told the committee: "All hotels need to have a policy designed to ensure room security and to implement it by training their staff."Emma Lingley-Clark, chief executive of the Suzy Lamplugh Trust, argued that guest safety should be treated like other basic standards expected of hotels.She said: "This should be considered in exactly the same light."'Culture change'Travelodge's interim chief executive Ray Reidy apologised again to the Maidenhead victim and others affected by the company's failings.He added: "Historically, speaking for Travelodge, I don't think we have taken it seriously. I don't think we did that intentionally. I don't think we'd deliberately ignored it. But I don't think we had given it, as highlighted in the report, the focus that it needed.""I would like to think that this is a milestone instance in the sector."We are still not where we want to be, but we are taking it incredibly seriously in terms of how we move forward."Speaking after the hearing, chair Olivia Bailey, who is also MP for Reading West and Mid Berkshire, said: "There have been lots of examples that we've seen in the media that people have told the committee of women's safety just not being taken seriously enough in hotels.""It is clear from the evidence we've heard today that not enough is being done. "There needs to be a wholesale culture change. "We need to make sure we don't just get warm words here. We need to make sure we have concrete action. "What we'll be doing as a committee is considering what that concrete action might need to look like".Kyran Smith was jailed in February for seven-and-a-half years following the Travelodge assault in December 2022.Get in touchDo you have a story BBC Berkshire should cover?

schema.headline: Hotels need minimum standards to keep women safe, committee told

title: Aaron Rodgers: Pittsburgh Steelers drop four-time MVP as starting quarterback
description: Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers may have played his last game in the NFL after being dropped by the Pittsburgh Steelers.In a brief statement publish
body: Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers may have played his last game in the NFL after being dropped by the Pittsburgh Steelers.In a brief statement published late on Tuesday local time, the Steelers said Mason Rudolph will be their starting quarterback for Friday's home game against the Denver Broncos.The Steelers added that Rodgers, the NFL's four-time Most Valuable Player, will be inactive for the game so will not serve as back-up to 31-year-old Rudolph.Rodgers, who turns 43 next week, was not listed on the Steelers' injury list on Tuesday and ESPN reports, external leaving him out was a coaching decision.The quarterback appeared on US sports TV programme the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday and confirmed his time with the Steelers was over."That ship has sailed," he said.He was also critical of Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, accusing him of snoring while he slept through team meetings.McCarthy was in charge of the Green Bay Packers for most of Rodgers' 18-year spell in Wisconsin, including their Super Bowl win in 2011.Rodgers, who joined Pittsburgh in 2025 after two years with the New York Jets, was "99% sure" he was going to retire after leading the Steelers to last season's play-offs.However, McCarthy's appointment by Pittsburgh persuaded him to play one more year.Although the Steelers have a 6-4 record, they have suffered two straight defeats after losing 19-16 at the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday.When asked about a potential change on Monday, McCarthy said "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback".But a day later the Steelers announced that is no longer the case.Pittsburgh's 29-word statement,, external published at 23:10 local time, could be an unceremonious end to an illustrious career.While Rodgers was unable to claim a second Super Bowl win, he was named the season MVP in 2011, 2014, 2020 and 2021. Only Peyton Manning (five) has won the award more times.Rodgers insisted his 22nd year in the NFL would be his last, and he has been benched at a crucial stage in the season.The Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) lead the AFC North division, with Pittsburgh third, but with seven games left the Steelers occupy the final play-off spot for the AFC Conference.Although Pittsburgh are 6-4, they have had to grind out some of those wins as they have struggled offensively. They rank 22nd for both points and passing yards per game.Rodgers is undoubtedly past his best, but his form has only dropped slightly from last season and the team's struggles are by no means entirely down to him.The Steelers' depth among their wide receivers is thin. Michael Pittman is out injured and DK Metcalf has not delivered the production expected when he was brought in with Rodgers before the 2025 season.Metcalf, 28, was even ejected during Sunday's loss at Philadelphia, meaning Rodgers had to lean on debutant Max Hurleman with the game on the line.And it is not as if Pittsburgh had a hot-shot rookie quarterback pushing for an opportunity to impress.Rudolph is in his ninth season and has started each as a back-up. After being drafted by the Steelers in 2018, he joined Tennessee for the 2024 season then returned to Pittsburgh, starting 19 of his 38 career games.McCarthy is hoping Rudolph can spark his offence, but if he doesn't, would they revert to Rodgers or try the two young quarterbacks on their roster?It would be some U-turn for the Steelers to ask the veteran to step back in after what has to be considered a chastening demotion, a move the team knew would grab headlines.Teams seldom make such a sudden change at this stage in the season, especially those with a winning record and a quarterback of Rodgers' stature.Rodgers has clashed with team management, team-mates and coaches throughout his career - including McCarthy - so would he be willing to come to his aid if asked? His comments on Wednesday suggest not.Whatever happens over the coming weeks, this is certainly not the farewell one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time was hoping for.

schema.headline: Aaron Rodgers: Pittsburgh Steelers drop four-time MVP as starting quarterback

title: Two men charged with trying to steal cufflinks and clock from royal home
description: Two men charged with trespassing at the Prince and Princess of Wales's country home are accused of trying to steal cufflinks and a clock.Police were c
body: Two men charged with trespassing at the Prince and Princess of Wales's country home are accused of trying to steal cufflinks and a clock.Police were called to Anmer Hall, on the Sandringham estate in Norfolk, shortly before 18:00 GMT on Monday after reports of suspicious activity.Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, both of no fixed address, have been charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site.Both appeared at Norwich Magistrates' Court earlier and have been remanded in custody until a hearing on Monday. Prosecutors said a third suspect remained at large. The men, who appeared in court in black sweatshirts, are accused of stealing six pairs of cufflinks and a clock.Both spoke through an Albanian interpreter, but did not enter pleas.The court heard one of the pairs of cufflinks were described as "the Duke of Edinburgh cufflinks".

schema.headline: Two men charged with trying to steal cufflinks and clock from royal home

title: Motorcycle catch: Man who caught a cricket ball on a moving vehicle found
description: "I told my friend riding the motorcycle to duck his head. I'm going to catch it."These are the words of Mehran Khan, who amazed sports fans around the
body: "I told my friend riding the motorcycle to duck his head. I'm going to catch it."These are the words of Mehran Khan, who amazed sports fans around the world when he caught a cricket ball while sitting on the back of a moving motorcycle.Mehran was passing a match in the Swat Premier League in Mingora when a ball sailed out of the ground towards him, with the passenger reaching out to catch it one-handed.Speaking to the BBC, he said of the grab, which has gone viral online: "I didn't think I would actually catch it." The employee of the Public Health Engineering Department was on his way home from work when he saw the ball being struck."I'm a cricket fan. I play cricket myself and I watch it too. I saw that Abrar Lala was at the crease and then he hit a six," he said."I told him [the friend who was driving] to duck his head. I'm going to catch it. Then I caught it."I made the effort, but I didn't expect to catch it. I thought it would fall somewhere nearby, but by the grace of God I managed to catch it."According to Mehran, immediately after the catch the Swat Premier League organisers announced a prize of 10,000 Pakistani rupees (about £27.60) for him, funded by the Pakistan Army.The Marghazar resident was caught by surprise when the recording of the catch spread so quickly online, saying: "The video went viral overnight. I didn't even know about it."He expressed his happiness at receiving the award, saying he was grateful to God, and added that he had returned the ball after taking the catch."People are saying I was taking the ball away with me, but that's not true. I returned it," he said.Swat Strikers won the match against GKR Dir by 34 runs, and Mehran urged the organisers to continue holding the tournament every year, describing it as an "excellent competition".

schema.headline: Motorcycle catch: Man who caught a cricket ball on a moving vehicle found
